description: We are a multidisciplinary team of engineering students specializing in biomedical, aeronautical, mechatronics, and systems engineering. Our project, H.E.A.R.T. (Health Evaluation & Astronaut Response Telemetry), is health monitoring software that tracks astronauts' vital signs in real time and detects early warning signs during space missions. Our team is complete, and we are fully committed to delivering a rigorous, innovative, and mission-ready solution.
summary: H.E.A.R.T is an offline-first health console that helps astronauts understand their own health on deep-space missions. On Mars, a radio message takes up to about 20 minutes one way, so Earth cannot help in real time. H.E.A.R.T compares each crew member with their own baseline instead of population averages and combines indicators (HRV, sleep, temperature, mood, hydration, radiation dose, balance) into patterns, flagging a possible early infection before fever appears. It shows a 3D body hologram whose organs change by status, an EVA readiness score (Ready / Review / Not fit), a crew view with contagion alerts and privacy switches, a solar-storm shelter checklist and cumulative radiation against NASA's 600 mSv limit. It answers the challenge by turning every astronaut into their own first responder. All data is simulated and thresholds are illustrative; it is not for clinical use.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. H.E.A.R.T is an offline-first health console for astronauts. It compares each crew member with their own baseline (mission days 1-14) and combines indicators (HRV, sleep, temperature, mood, hydration, exercise, radiation dose, balance) into patterns, so it can flag a possible early infection before fever appears. It shows an interactive 3D body hologram whose organs change by status, a readiness score for critical tasks such as an EVA (Ready / Review / Not fit), a crew view with contagion alerts and per-astronaut privacy switches, a solar-storm shelter checklist, cumulative radiation against the 600 mSv career limit, and a medical packet to Earth that shows the communication delay.

HOW IT WORKS. A seeded generator creates 180 days of simulated data for four fictional crew roles. A deterministic alert engine compares every metric with the member's baseline, detects combined patterns, derives a status per organ and computes readiness. The interface renders that result; the 3D hologram colours organs by status. Every deviation follows the same three steps: verify the measurement, apply the countermeasure, re-evaluate or send telemetry to Earth. No generative AI makes medical decisions.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT. On a Mars mission a radio message takes up to about 20 minutes one way, so Earth cannot help in real time. H.E.A.R.T aims to let every astronaut understand their own health, decide what to do, and know when to involve the crew or flight surgeons. It also supports the Crew Medical Officer with a view of the whole crew, including contagion risk.

CREATIVITY. We compare people with their own baseline, not population averages. We detect combined patterns instead of isolated numbers, following NASA's point that spaceflight hazards feed each other. Status is never colour-only (circle, triangle, diamond, always with text). Check-in rewards completing measurements, never "good" values, so nobody has a reason to hide symptoms. A 2-minute demo mode tells the whole story inside the real app.

TOOLS. JavaScript (vanilla ES modules), Vite, Three.js (WebGL 3D anatomy, with a Canvas 2D fallback), SVG, a service worker for offline use, GitHub Pages for hosting. 3D anatomy derived from BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan). Fonts bundled via Fontsource. No special hardware: it runs in any modern browser. Code was written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED. Medical thresholds are illustrative and labelled so; all data is simulated; the prototype is not for clinical use. Accessibility (keyboard access, ARIA labels, contrast, reduced motion), a Spanish/English toggle, privacy controls, so it works offline.
